newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas ends firmer, most business done in May.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas ends firmer, most business done in May.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract was quieter in the afternoon session than in the morning on Wednesday, and the main interest was centred on the May contract, as it had been in the morning.

By the close of trade, a total of 215 lots had been traded, of which 160 were in May. And 50 of those May trades were done in the afternoon session - more than was concluded in all months over the whole day on Monday.

A futures broker said he thought two main players had been responsible for most of the May deals. "It's the same players doing all the trade," he said. He added that most interest on the OTC market had centred on the third quarter, although on futures there were only four deals totalling 25 lots in the individual months making up the third quarter.

Prices were firmer across the board. May fell slightly in the afternoon, but the last trade still showed an increase of 0.125 pence a therm from the previous settlement price, up to 10.275 pence. And most of the other traded months, June, July, August, September and December, were also up, by as much as 0.350 pence a therm.
The only exception was October, which traded once at 12.50 pence, unchanged from the previous settlement level.
Unusually, the bulk of trade was done in the morning, with 145 of the 215 lots traded done then and only 70 lots added in the two-hour afternoon session. Normally this pattern is reversed.
